blocking: Desktop accordion fallback can clip ceremony descriptions when site.js fails: collapsed bodies retain absolute positioning inside overflow-hidden panels.
The stylesheet identifies the deployed Latin font as a trial file requiring replacement before launch.

fixes.what: Reset every accordion body to position:relative; inset:auto; pointer-events:auto, and let each panel grow with its expanded details.
fixes.why: The fallback restores visibility but leaves desktop positioning and pointer restrictions that can clip text and prevent Read more interaction.

fixes.what: Replace the documented trial asset with the licensed production TT Ramillas Bold webfont.
fixes.why: The source explicitly marks this asset as unfinished launch work.

fixes.what: Draw keyboard focus on the panel using :has(.accordion__trigger:focus-visible), above its body and media layers.
fixes.why: The trigger's focus outline sits at z-index 2 beneath the open body at z-index 3, making the indicator vulnerable to obscuring.

fixes.what: Use the same desktop threshold for navigation CSS and desktopQuery, and close the drawer when crossing that threshold.
fixes.why: CSS switches navigation at 768px while JavaScript switches at 769px; resizing an open drawer to exactly 768px hides its toggle without clearing the drawer state.

fixes.where: assets/js/site.js — accordion open(), settle(), and ResizeObserver
fixes.what: Reserve enough desktop row height for the tallest expanded description at the current width, recalculating after fonts load and viewport changes.
fixes.why: The current height lock ends after each hover transition, allowing differing description heights to move all following sections and refresh scroll animations.
